title: Chapter 46: A Demonical Flash
content:
Chapter 46:

A Demonical Flash

They faced each other for only a few seconds, but to Subaru, that silent stretch felt like it lasted for hours.

Rem’s eyes, which seemed to have lost all reason, regained their emotion after a sudden blink.

“—Sister, and Subaru?”

At her surprised voice, Subaru let out a sigh of relief. Ram stirred in his arms, her eyes snapping open.

“Ah, Rem, you had me worried. You shouldn’t just run off on your own like that.”

“Rem apologizes, Sister. She was just desperate to do something…”

“Even if you don’t push yourself so hard, we’ve found a way to manage. If we just use Barusu here as a decoy, everything will be peachy.”

“Ah! Of course! To think there was such a play! Rem is moved to tears!”

The twins ran to each other and joined hands. Communicating with an unprecedented synchronization rate, they looked at him with eyes full of expectation, prompting Subaru to thump his chest.

“Well, leave it to me. I’ll show you the greatest decoy performance of the century!”

““Kyaa, wonderful! What a man, truly worthy of Lady Emilia!!””

Cheered on enthusiastically by the two of them, Subaru responded with immense pride.

This long loop of hardship was finally over. Having brilliantly grasped the light of hope he’d seen, Natsuki Subaru set off on the path to glory—.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

“Or so the ideal scenario would’ve gone.”

Grumbling in a pathetic voice, Subaru slowly edged backward, completely discarding that delusional turn of events.

Directly in front of him, the eyes of Rem staring his way held no trace of the emotion that had returned in his fantasy; all that existed there was an earnest, pitch-black murderous intent.

By no stretch of the imagination did she look to be in a state of mind where a conversation was possible.

Every single drop of sweat felt as heavy as lead. The weight of the sweat clinging to his eyelashes threatened to block his vision, and Subaru tried to endure it by blinking one eye at a time.

He’d had enough of blinking both eyes at once, creating an opening, and paying the painful price during his fight with a witchbeast.

—Realizing that the very fact he was having such thoughts meant he was treating the Rem before him as an enemy, Subaru gave a bitter smile. Just what exactly had he thrown himself into this place to do?

“Reeeem-rin. It’s your buddy, Suuuubaru.”

To shake himself out of his unknowingly rising vigilance, and at the same time to break the suffocating silence, he deliberately acted cheerful as he called out to her.

In response to Subaru’s friendly greeting, Rem’s reaction was—

“Don't give me that fiery gaze, I might just get burned.”

With a snap so sharp it practically made a sound, she whipped her head around and locked onto him.

Until then, she had at least been glaring around her surroundings, but now he could tell she had completely fixated on him as her target. He might have messed up.

The demonic aura radiating from Rem’s current figure was so tremendous it made him think so.

Her entire body in that familiar maid uniform was covered in splattered blood—and because she had been bathed in fresh, wet blood over blood that had already dried, the two-tone color of dark, murky red and vivid red only accentuated the gruesomeness. Perhaps due to a physical change from her Oni transformation, bluish-green veins pulsed visibly beneath the white skin peeking out from her torn sleeves, and the nails on both her hands had grown as terrifyingly sharp as those of the witchbeasts.

The “self-defense” iron ball hanging from her right arm was still perfectly intact, having clearly been blessed with as many opportunities to be swung as her exploits suggested. Coated in caked blood and various other substances, its sheer brutality seemed to have been cranked up another notch.

He could say this with absolute certainty.

The only reason he was able to maintain any semblance of composure was because he had prepared himself for Rem’s state to some extent. If he were to unexpectedly run into the current Rem on a dark road at night, he would absolutely wet his pants.

Yet, despite exposing herself to such madness, the white horn protruding from her forehead—and only that—maintained a pure white beauty, as if completely ignorant to the carnage around it.

Even though it was the most symbolic part that made Rem a vicious “Oni,” that horn alone gave Subaru an impression of being terribly out of place.

However, the situation wasn’t exactly considerate of Subaru’s feelings.

Looking around, the witchbeasts that had fallen to the bottom of the valley and scattered were also keeping a distance from which they could observe them from behind rocks and deep within the trees.

They were likely gauging the movements of Subaru and the others, as well as Rem. If they decided they were easy prey, it was easy to imagine them joining the fray once more.

For Subaru, who was at the absolute bottom of the power balance, their entry into the battle would be equivalent to literal certain death. Because of that, it was no exaggeration to say that Rem’s next move was his lifeline.

Gulping, he closed his eyes for a second, and then stared straight back into Rem’s gaze.

What fluctuations of emotion would her eyes, those twin irises glaring at him, show? He poured his entire soul into his gaze, determined not to miss even a fragment of it.

And then—

“Sister…”

It was a hoarse, utterly exhausted voice.

But it was a definite sound that vibrated against Subaru’s eardrums.

With trembling lips, as if bewildered, Rem’s eyes were fixed intently on Ram’s profile. There was a genuine, positive emotion there, and Subaru marveled at that fact.

Even while in the midst of surrendering to a combat instinct fierce enough to strip away her sanity, her consciousness clearly perceived the figure of her other half, the sister she loved and respected so deeply.

“You truly are the shining example of a siscon. I’m just glad we could meet up. From here on…”

“

LET GO

.”

The tail end of his sentence being cut off and the iron ball flying at him wrapped in a gale-force wind happened at the exact same time.

The fact that he was able to instantly tilt his body to the right was nothing short of a miracle.

It was fortunate that the laceration on his right calf had slightly broken Subaru’s posture as he tried to step forward.

A spike on the passing iron ball grazed his left shoulder, and his brain boiled with the agonizing pain of his flesh being gouged out.

His throat trembled from the pain, but he didn’t have the time to let it consume his consciousness.

Stepping diagonally forward—

“I said that hurts!!”

Spinning his body from the side of his gouged, bleeding shoulder, Subaru sidestepped, slipping under the chain of the overextended iron ball. A split second later, the sweeping chain fiercely struck the spot where Subaru had just been, carving the distinct pattern of an iron snake into the earth.

It wasn’t hard to imagine that if his evasion had been delayed, the flesh on Subaru’s back would have exploded in that exact same pattern.

Shuddering at the imagined pain of his skin being ripped open, Subaru looked at Rem imploringly.

However, there was no change in her posture as she directed her gaze at him. Her eyes, drenched in hostility, were as vacuous as ever; it was safe to judge that she had lost her mind, just as it looked.

“So she went Oni mode, but it’s an uncontrollable setting, huh…”

From her current behavior, Subaru made that guess.

If that was the case, the issue now was verifying the differences from last night. Rem should have undergone her Oni transformation the exact same way last night, but at that point, she seemed to have regained her senses immediately.

Was the issue the amount of time that had passed, or was it caused by a shocking, eye-opening sight?

If Subaru protecting her and getting severely injured right in front of her had affected her mind that much—

“Should I try taking a hit from the iron ball? I’d be instant mincemeat, though…”

If recreating the same conditions as last night would do it, he was sure she would snap out of it.

Except Subaru would be ground meat in exchange.

“The next best plan… getting super-chomped by the dogs.”

If he threw himself on the ground in total prostration, those pests hiding in the rocks would go “What kind of wild beasts would we be to turn down a free meal!” and gladly come feast on him. He felt like it could work, but there was no guarantee Rem would overlook a defenseless Subaru, and on top of that, it would just turn into a bargain sale of overwritten curses that would thus massively defeat the point.

At worst, Rem would just abandon him to the very end, resulting in a ‘Predation Ending’—he could practically see the word “Dog’s Death” flashing before his eyes.

Following this pessimistic train of thought, he was truly out of options.

Ram, who might understand the situation, was still far from conscious. He had been shaking her for a while now, trying to see if she would somehow come back, but it looked like it would take time before that had any effect.

Neither Rem in front of him nor the ulgarms surrounding them seemed likely to wait for that.

Subaru licked off the sweat running down his cheek, moistened his lips, and let his mouth run.

If he couldn’t think of any viable moves, he’d just try to cover every typical trope for interacting with someone who had lost their mind. To begin with, brute-forcing his options was the only way to find a breakthrough.

In that case, doing exactly that was the Subaru way—.

“Hey, Rem. Listen me, you coldhearted girl who doesn’t quite know who I am. Let’s have a happy, embarrassing Treasure 

Time

1

 to figure that out. Right, thinking back, it was three days ago. Tackling the laundry with weirdly high energy, I stood before the designated laundry basket and couldn't help but surge with excitement... WHOA!!”

He attempted a comeback with a bonding talk that appealed to emotion and memory, but it was immediately cut short by an interruption from the short-tempered Rem.

The whirling iron ball came flying, snapping and shattering the trees in its path, closing in while scattering wood splintered everywhere. He barely dodged it with a diving forward roll. Taking pains not to drop Ram, he gracefully dodged the chain’s subsequent pursuit with a hop, step, and a jump. Turning around—

“Taking your bludgeoning turn in the middle of someone’s story is terrible manners, you know?! I wonder what your family must be like… Oh, here she is right here!”

“Give… Sister… back…!”

Rem muttered, leaning forward toward Subaru as he looked down at Ram in his arms and shouted. Or so he thought. Suddenly, using only the swing of her arm, she yanked back the thrown iron ball, and using the recoil from that swing, she spun sharply—

“—!”

Rem’s spinning back kick landed a direct hit on the torso of a witchbeast attempting to pounce from behind—a roar resembling an explosion erupted, and even from a distance, it was obvious that the insides of the blasted-away ulgarm had been mashed to a pulp.

It had tried to swoop in and steal the kill and look where that got it.

The witchbeasts, who had been planning to launch wave attacks in tandem with their vanguard’s approach, involuntarily halted at the sight of its gruesome death.

Which, in other words, was a folly equivalent to lying on their backs and exposing their bellies in front of a hunter.

A sideways sweeping blow crushed the belly of one and the head of another beast side by side into a single lumped mess. Paying no mind to the scattering chunks of meat, Rem stepped forward, riding the momentum of that strike. With her forward step, she crushed the foreleg of a cowering witchbeast beneath her foot, and with its movement stopped, her other foot kicked up into its snout—a light snapping sound rang out as the witchbeast’s cervical vertebrae twisted in an impossible direction and shattered.

Without stopping, Rem leaped right in front of the final beast in the attack wave. Grabbing the terrified creature by the scruff of its neck, she didn’t do anything special, just chucked it straight up into the sky with all her might.

Tracing a parabola, the frail howl of the witchbeast, now turned into a fastball, trailed off and echoed. It grew fainter and fainter, then louder and louder, before abruptly cutting off with a sound like fruit being smashed against solid ground.

Massacre after massacre. Slaughter for the sake of slaughter. Carnage within carnage.

No other thoughts came to mind regarding the acts performed right in front of him.

An overwhelming difference in power, rendering it akin to a child’s play.

Their very standing as living creatures was different. Between “Oni” and “witchbeast,” they might compete in ominousness, but they could never contest in terms of absolute supremacy.

Even so, Subaru absolutely couldn’t understand the witchbeasts challenging an “Oni” they couldn’t possibly beat. Their limbs trembled in terror, they raised anguished howls in the face of death, and they clearly felt grief and indignation at the discarded corpses of their kin—yet they never, ever tried to flee from the fight.

Perhaps that was the very core of what made them “witchbeasts”—entities birthed by the hands of the Witch, earning them the title of foreign enemies who bring harm to humanity.

Witnessing that reckless charge—which, in a sense, was a spectacle of proactive suicide—Subaru furrowed his brows at a sudden doubt that surfaced in his mind.

Rem’s figure, flattening and pulverizing the pack of witchbeasts with overwhelming tyranny.

He doubted whether her terrifying combat prowess, as seen from the sidelines, had even been exercised to its full potential in the two or so attacks she had already directed his way.

Not to brag, but Subaru had a fair amount of confidence in his own athletic abilities.

When it came to gymnastics, there were almost no moves he couldn’t do, like back handsprings or somersaults, and he held records that put him far above the national average in agility.

However, if you asked whether Subaru’s physical capabilities were superior when compared to witchbeasts living in the wild, he couldn’t bring himself to believe he won in agility, explosive power, or stamina. The best he could do was maybe win in a contest of pure strength, but even that wasn’t a definite yes when he recalled the experience of momentarily being pinned down by brute force.

For Subaru, who had handed down such a somewhat disappointing self-evaluation, the absolute trampling Rem was carrying out right before his eyes was not something within a realm he could possibly evade.

A strike that witchbeasts couldn’t dodge and were turned into mincemeat by—Subaru should naturally be taking those hits too. And yet, there was the contradiction of him having already successfully survived twice. Thinking it through, Subaru found a thread there, once again too thin to rely on.

“If she’s aware of Ram’s presence even after losing her mind, that means…”

Looking down at the girl letting out pained sleeping breaths in his arms, he gently brushed aside the bangs falling over her forehead with his fingers.

Every flying iron ball was on an instant-kill trajectory aimed from Subaru’s neck up. But looking at it another way, it was a manifestation of her will not to kill anyone other than Subaru.

Because Subaru was holding Ram, Rem was pulling her punches.

Therefore, her mercilessness towards the witchbeasts and the attacks directed at him were disproportionate in their severity.

Having formed that deduction, Subaru instinctively held his breath.

If that guess was correct, they just might get through this.

—They might just be able to cross this seemingly quite hopeless situation, albeit via a precarious method akin to walking across a frayed tightrope on the verge of snapping.

“And to do that—”

He looked around.

The current layout of the valley floor had Subaru in the center. To the north, Rem stood with her back to the cliff, while the ulgarms formed an encircling net broadly scattered to the east and west.

From the witchbeasts’ perspective, both Subaru and Rem should be equal prey, but the current situation made it seem like they were prioritizing Rem due to her danger level. Rem was also paying a certain amount of attention to Subaru, but she was too busy dealing with the attacking witchbeasts to launch an offensive.

However, it was easy to imagine that once the number of witchbeasts interfering with her actions thinned out, Rem would direct her fangs toward Subaru in order to take back her sister.

Taking all that into account, there was only one action for Subaru to take.

Steeling his resolve, he spread his legs wide, took a deep breath, and stared fixedly at Rem.

—Take the leap, me. Guts for men, charm for women.

“So stop making that scary face and smile, Rem. —I can Return…”

The second stoppage of the world today, and the banquet of screams caused by the black haze swirling from it.

Even if he had prepared himself for the intense pain that would occur, it wasn’t something he could endure. Much less so when it was accompanied by the appearance of not just one hand, but a left hand as well.

Perhaps having gotten a taste of success upon completion of its right arm, in front of Subaru, who had his unmoving eyelids forced wide open, the sensation of slipping through his sternum and caressing his innards had transformed into the feeling of two palms.

One grasped his heart, and the other palm gently touched Subaru’s cheek, as if treating him as something precious. —A chill welled up, and immediately after, pain thoroughly ravaged his nerves.

Agony, agony, agony—!

The world flipped upside down, accompanied by a colossal sense of disgust as if all his stomach contents were being mashed and stirred around simultaneously. He was ceasing to be himself. A sickening sensation as if every single part of him, from the top of his head to the tips of his toes, was being wholesale replaced. The numbness of nerves no longer being able to perceive nerves as nerves boiled his brain, his consciousness gradually muddying. Yet, only the sensation of the soft palm touching his cheek was warm, carrying a sense of relief that felt as if it could melt away both his body and soul radiating from that spot. But Subaru knew a feeling that surpassed that without needing to rely on it, so—.

“I’m… back.”

His vision blurred. His soul was worn down. Yet he hadn’t brought any pain or suffering back to reality.

No time had passed either. Before his eyes was the same chaotic scene, with the witchbeasts and Rem still locked in their back-and-forth standoff—however, the moment Subaru returned to this side, a massive change occurred in that confrontation.

As if something colossal that could not be ignored had suddenly appeared in this place, the attention of both Rem and the pack of ulgarms turned toward him.

Exactly as planned, the cause was likely the fact that the Witch’s scent enveloping Subaru had surged to another level.

—Rem roared.

To snatch back her beloved sister from the hostile entity emitting such a tremendous lingering scent of the Witch.

—The ulgarms began to bay all at once.

As their instincts were lured by that nostalgic scent, seeking to gather the entire pack within the forest.

—Subaru also howled.

Dodging the pouncing claws of the witchbeasts and the smashed-in iron ball with a hair’s breadth of timing, as if seeking to set fire to his own life and soul.

※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

The chaotic melee began.

An Oni, witchbeasts, and an ordinary guy. While bearing the burden of an existence completely out of place without even needing to calmly think about it, Subaru continued to dance in the center of the free-for-all, paying meticulous attention to his surroundings.

Subaru’s actions were consistently simple.

Maintain a distance that was neither too close nor too far from where the battle was intensifying, and dedicate all his energy solely to dodging the sparks that flew his way—that was all.

Once again, right before his eyes, a witchbeast was struck by the iron ball and quickly transformed into a stain on the rock wall. Undeterred by the death of their kin, however, the witchbeasts formed coordinated groups of three, fiercely attacking in an attempt to inflict a deep wound on Rem. Their shallow cunning was in vain; their leaps were intercepted by swatting hand motions, and starting from the ones whose movements had been halted, they fell prey to her descending murder weapon.

Observing this out of the corner of his eye, Subaru readjusted his grip on Ram, who was slipping, and leapt backward. He narrowly escaped a diving witchbeast, throwing himself into Rem’s striking distance.

And then came the interception from Rem, who had sharply noticed his approach. He avoided her thrusting iron handle by braking to an abrupt halt, ducked under the delayed flying chain by crouching down, and the iron ball passing overhead made a bright red flower bloom on the head of the witchbeast closing in from behind him.

Confirming just that, he threw away all shame and appearances, making a mad dash to escape in a ground-crawling, cockroach-style scramble. Witchbeasts obstructed Rem as she tried to give chase, and he succeeded in breaking away.

Maintaining a certain distance, he let out a sigh of relief, praising his own judgment that had just saved his life.

“—Hah! I’m actually doing pretty well, aren’t I?”

Bouncing around desperately so the dogs wouldn’t bite him, shoving the dogs chasing him onto a maid girl, and crawling away like a cockroach to escape the angry girl’s temper tantrum.

Simply putting it into words yielded only that much substance, making him mildly want to die, but he rationalized that he was doing it to not die, and rather beautified the disgraceful display in his mind.

At present, the strategy Subaru had envisioned was going well. Both in terms of buying time and reducing the total number of ulgarms, it wasn’t a bad development.

Glancing up, he felt the presence of packs of witchbeasts gathering toward them from multiple directions leading to the valley floor.

Subaru’s body odor, which had spread across a considerable area of the forest, continued to incessantly stimulate the ulgarms’ instincts. A sinful tale indeed.

Therefore, there was a chance of survival.

He ended up feeling this premature joy, even though the situation hadn’t actually improved at all.

“—Uh?”

It came suddenly.

A new pack of ulgarms entered the valley floor, throwing themselves into the death struggle with Rem. While witnessing that sight, the very moment he tried to lightly shake his body to prepare for evasive action, a sensation akin to dizziness caused Subaru’s posture to collapse severely.

His knees buckled, and he almost fell forward. Instinctively, he flipped over to protect Ram’s body in his arms, crashing into the ground on his injured left shoulder. A groan escaped his throat, stifled by the sharp pain, but what dominated Subaru’s consciousness far more than that was—

“This chill…”

He remembered it, an extraordinary chill that seemed to freeze him from the core of his body.

Even after pushing his body with his life on the line and challenging this battlefield with his soul ablaze, it was an interference that felt like throwing cold water on all that fervor.

Feeling that, Subaru regretted his own blunder yet again.

The more numbers he gathered like this, the greater the danger became. Given that the entity right in front of them was so overwhelmingly powerful, if they decided they needed even a little bit more strength, resuming the suspended curse should have been the very first option that came to mind for them.

He cast his gaze around.

One of the ulgarms participating in this fray was activating the curse cast on Subaru and siphoning his mana. Yet, looking around, there was no sign of any witchbeast looking the part. More importantly, he was in no position to even imagine what state a witchbeast would be in while activating a curse.

And with a body that now found it a chore to move even a single finger, even if he were able to identify the source of the curse, stopping its curse arts—even at the cost of a mutual kill—seemed impossible.

“…Is it all over?”

After coming this far, would everything vanish in vain?

Subaru’s consciousness began to fade from the increasingly intense chill. He reached out to somehow cling onto it, but no matter how far he stretched, his hand vainly clawed at the air—.

Abruptly, the chill vanished, and blood flow returned to his palm.

—A deafening roar. It echoed at the exact same time Subaru’s condition returned to normal.

Forcing open his hazing vision, Subaru let his gaze wander in search of the sound’s origin. And then, deep within the forest, he saw the figure of Rem, who had stamped the ground heavily and slammed her iron ball into the bedrock. Beneath that flail, he also saw the exploded corpse of a single witchbeast exposed for all to see.

Realizing the causal relationship between his remarkably recovered physical condition and that situation, Subaru stood up.

The witchbeast Rem had just crushed to a pulp was the one executing the curse on Subaru. Because its life had been snuffed out, the execution of the curse must have been interrupted.

What a terrifying coincidence; he felt almost charmed by how incredibly lucky he was—.

“Like hell it is.”

Her current position was a vast distance away from where she had been standing just moments ago.

Ignoring the witchbeasts dotting the path to get there, there was only one reason to snipe that specific one.

Shaking off everything, sustaining lacerations from claws while dashing through, Rem pinpointed the single beast that had activated the curse and struck it down.

Subaru wasn’t so dense as to not understand what that meant.

Even if she had lost her sanity, even in a mental state where she didn’t know who Subaru was.

Rem would not mistake her beloved sister, nor had she forgotten her initial purpose for diving into the forest.

If so, he thought.

Conscious of what he had to do, Subaru rubbed his eyelids.

He felt he shouldn’t be using her in this deceptive manner, but rather following his original objective. Ultimately,

“The initial ideal vision. A heart-pounding joint curse extermination operation with the maid sisters, Ram and Rem.”

Only if they could do that did Subaru gauge they had a chance to make it back alive from this curse-riddled situation.

Therefore, he had to bring back Rem’s sanity. Because the one Subaru needed wasn’t an “Oni,” but her—the one who was politely impudent, prone to jumping to conclusions, given to snap judgments, and constantly causing trouble.

“—The horn.”

Suddenly, that voice vibrated Subaru’s eardrums from right beside him.

Looking down, Ram, still held in his arms, had opened her eyes slightly, her lips moving in the gaps of her hazy consciousness.

“You awake?”

“Ram figured now… was the most perfect timing…”

“Yeah, you’ve got great instincts, onee-sama. —‘The horn,’ did you say?”

Ram managed a small smile; Subaru asked back, also surfacing a smile that was half-bravado, half-defiant. At that, she pulled her chin back sluggishly,

“What makes Rem an Oni is that horn… so if you hit it with one strong, clean strike… that will bring her back…”

“Are you sure?”

“It should. Probably. Ram would hope so.”

“You’re being too vague on that, no?! But I’m gonna believe you.”

Declaring so, Subaru looked at Rem’s figure.

The white horn growing from her forehead was roughly ten centimeters long. If he imagined Puck standing on her forehead, the size was fairly close.

—Right there, one clean strike.

“Doesn’t that seem way impossible?”

“Muster up your wisdom and courage, and figure something out.”

“Actually, I’ve just thought of a method to maybe reach it if I muster up my wisdom and courage.”

Ram raised an eyebrow in surprise at Subaru’s response.

Subaru gave her a bitter smile, twisting his lips as if hesitant to say it,

“But I’m sure you’ll get mad.”

“If it brings my sister back to her senses, Ram won’t get mad.”

“Really?”

“Truly, really.”

“Swear on Ros-chi?”

“…You’re quite the daredevil to go with that. Yes, Ram swears on Master Roswaal.”

Since Ram declared it so thoroughly manfully, Subaru decided to respect her opinion.

In front of him, Rem turned back his way with relaxed movements.

The core of her consciousness was still directed at him, while her expanding net of vigilance was on the surrounding ulgarms.

Against this Rem in an omnidirectional alert posture, Subaru made his move to strike her horn.

That was—

“Ooooh, hup!”

“—Huh?”

Twisting his body, lowering his hips into a stance, and swinging his arms while rotating his entire body with the recoil—he threw Ram’s body, which he had been carrying in both arms, in a massive toss right at Rem.

She must never have expected to be thrown.

The dumbfounded face of Ram dancing through the air drifted farther away, being drawn toward Rem. As expected, even Rem in her Oni state seemed flabbergasted by this, but the instant she realized that the thing flying at her was her defenseless sister, she immediately let go of the iron flail and reached out her arms to secure her body.

Nimbly moving her fingers with their elongated claws, Rem caught her sister in her blood-soaked arms. In that split second, a gentle expression swiftly washed over the face that had been drenched in nothing but murderous intent.

—So as not to be late for witnessing that moment, Subaru’s body had propelled itself.

At the exact same time he threw Ram’s body, he dashed forcefully forward in the same direction. While Rem’s gaze was fixed on Ram flying above, he closed in, slipping through her blind spot while keeping low.

Stepping in, his right hand drew the sword from his waist, using that momentum to aim for the horn atop her head. Cutting through the wind, the timing caught her completely off guard.

Even Rem was unable to so much as react against this surprise attack—however,

“—Oof.”

By a tip’s worth that had chipped off his fully swung sword, and by a single step’s worth he had chickened out on in his powerful dash; under a situation so razor-thin, he ever so slightly failed to catch her horn.

Dumbfounded that a once-in-a-lifetime chance had slipped right through his fingers, Subaru cried out,

“I chickened out! Just one more step… I didn’t have enough courage!!”

His body spun from the momentum of his whiffed swing.

Right on the verge of turning his back, he saw out of the corner of his eye Rem’s left hand readied in a spear-hand strike. Simply thrusting that straight forward would open up a clean, breezy hole right through Subaru’s torso.

Once again by Rem’s hand—he bit his lip hard, thinking that was the one thing he absolutely didn’t want, when immediately after,

The ground beneath his feet exploded, and the resulting wave of earth and sand sent Subaru’s body flying spectacularly.

“Ooooooh—?!”

Pummeled by a shotgun blast of rocks, bleeding and feeling the pain of tearing skin, the airborne Subaru looked down and saw the reason for this disaster.

The explosion of the ground had come from the south of Subaru’s position, caused by the puppy witchbeast crouching there. The one he thought he hadn’t seen since they had fallen to the bottom of the valley had likely been waiting for the exact moment Subaru and Rem overlapped in its line of fire.

The instant it calculated it could finish off both of them at once, it deployed its magical force in a surprise attack, throwing in a flashy disruption with that wave of earth and sand.

However, that scheme—

“————!!”

Rem roared and delivered a single stomp against the exploding earth.

The wave of earth and sand that was about to rise up was offset by that sheer power, its effect reduced to merely rustling her blue bangs a little violently.

Canceling out magic by smashing it with pure violence—it couldn’t be quite that simple, but it was a method of crushing magic close to it.

Holding her caught sister delicately, Rem stepped to the side to escape the magical aftershocks. —She had completely forgotten about the existence of Subaru, who was fluttering down from above.

Spinning round and round, the vertically rotating world could by no means be perceived normally.

However, his right hand was still gripping the short sword tightly, and his landing spot had fortunately missed the rock wall; it was just plain, hard dirt.

And right directly below him was Rem, exposing her head, unaware of his presence.

There’d be nothing better than this, there’d be no more chances after this, he couldn’t hope for anything beyond this.

Raising the sword, gripping it with both hands, he prepared to channel every last ounce of his strength.

Stacking coincidence on top of coincidence, on top of coincidence, to see if he’d finally reach it.

Hooray for plot armor. Miracles were the best. The whims of God did their job once in a while.

—If anything, it would’ve been much cooler if it had worked during that earlier swing.

A wry smile. He had no time. Right up close, in a world that was slowly decelerating, there was Rem.

He could see the horn. He flipped the raised sword to use the blunt edge, and unleashed the pent-up power.

“Laugh, Rem. —Today, I’m more demonically possessed than a Demon.”

The blade he let loose, straight and true, the flash of the sword surged toward the white horn—.

The high-pitched sound of striking steel echoed sharply through the witchbeast forest.

Followed immediately by Subaru’s ungraceful scream from a botched landing.
